transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Jimenez (Redwood SE), Lina Zhang (Redwood CSM), Tom Everett (CedarPoint Head of MLOps), Priya Singh (Security Architect), Leon Wu (Data Engineer), Ava Moreno (Product Manager)

Summary:
Weekly pilot check-in focused on security/compliance and initial results. Discussed SSO integration status (SAML), audit log format/retention, data retention and masking options, SOC 2 artifacts, and next steps for enabling extended logging and a short dedicated-node latency run. Agreed on action items and timelines.

Topics covered:
- SSO/SAML exchange and IdP specifics
- Audit logging schema, retention, and evidence samples
- Data retention and redaction/masking of PII during the pilot
- SOC 2 Type II documentation and control mapping
- Pilot results: token costs, tail latency, and error incidents

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Patel: All right everybody, thanks for joining. Uh we're going to kick off, quick agenda, SSO status, audit logs, data retention, SOC two docs, then a brief review of the results from the last two weeks and next steps.
[00:18] Tom Everett: Thanks Maya. We got Leon and I on, Priya's on, and Ava. Uh we are mostly here to lock down the compliance bits so we can move to the next pilot phase.
[00:27] Carlos Jimenez: Hi everyone, Carlos from Redwood. Quick note, I pushed a branch earlier with the SAML metadata and a sample SP config, but I don't think it made it to your IdP team.
[00:37] Priya Singh: I saw an email, but yeah we haven't ingested the metadata. Our IdP team needs a few fields, specifically the assertion consumer URL and certificate thumbprint. Those were scrambled in the export, maybe whitespace issues.
[00:50] Carlos Jimenez: Got it. I can resend a cleaned bundle. Sorry about the whitespace; some exporters introduce line breaks in the cert. I'll sanitize and attach as a raw XML file.
[01:03] Lina Zhang: Quick clarification, Priya, are you going to use just SSO for admin console access or do you need it for API-level auth for service accounts too?
[01:12] Priya Singh: For now admin console and audit access. API-level keys we'll lock down separately. We don't want service account SAML mapped directly to prod tokens until we've validated session policies.
[01:24] Leon Wu: From an engineering perspective, we need to see the audit logs schema before we can wire the ELK pipeline. Can you confirm which events are logged?
[01:34] Carlos Jimenez: Yes, the staging cluster will emit events for auth:login, auth:token-issue, model:request:start, model:request:end, cache:hit/miss, and admin:config_change. Each event has timestamp, request id, user id if available, resource, model id, latency_ms, and status.
[01:52] Tom Everett: Are user ids PII? We need to know hashing or pseudonymization options.
[01:57] Carlos Jimenez: By default we emit the user principal as whatever the IdP provides. We can enable a hashing layer on the platform side to pseudonymize principal values. That's configurable per-tenant.
[02:08] Priya Singh: We'd prefer pseudonymization with salted hashing. Is the salt per-tenant or global?
[02:14] Carlos Jimenez: We support per-tenant salts; that will make cross-tenant correlation impossible. I'll include the config options in the sample logs.
[02:23] [00:02:30] Maya Patel: Quick interjection — on SOC 2 evidence, we should share a redacted version of our Type II report and the control mapping doc. I can do that after legal checks.
[02:36] Priya Singh: We'll want the control mapping mapped to our own control IDs, otherwise our auditors will ask for traceability.
[02:42] Lina Zhang: We have a mapping template that most customers fill out; Maya, I'll send you the template so we can produce the mapping faster.
[02:51] Maya Patel: Perfect.
[02:54] [00:03:00] Carlos Jimenez: On data retention, the platform currently supports 30/90/365/never retention buckets for raw request logs and a separate retention policy for cached KV payloads. For this pilot we recommended 90 days.
[03:12] Tom Everett: Our security policy wants 90 days for logs but only 30 days for raw payloads containing user-generated content unless masked. Can you do that split?
[03:22] Carlos Jimenez: Yes, that's possible. We'll need to enable payload redaction for message bodies, that's a toggle and also an optional field-based masker for JSON payloads.
[03:34] Leon Wu: How does redaction affect debugging? If we red... redact the payload, will you still store prompt embeddings for debugging cost analysis?
[03:44] Carlos Jimenez: Embeddings are derived artifacts; you can choose to keep embeddings but with separate retention. Some customers keep embeddings for 90 days but redact prompts to 30. We can do that.
[03:55] [00:04:00] Priya Singh: About encryption at rest — do you have customer-managed keys?
[04:02] Carlos Jimenez: For Private deployments yes. For Redwood Hosted we support integration with AWS KMS and customer-managed CMKs. Right now the pilot uses Redwood-managed keys, but if you need CMK we can escalate for the pilot to use a dedicated CMK.
[04:16] Priya Singh: We'd like a dedicated CMK for this pilot. Will that change SLAs?
[04:21] Maya Patel: There might be slight provisioning delay but not SLA change. I'll note that as a next step.
[04:27] [00:04:30] Ava Moreno: On the pilot results: we saw cost/unit roughly in line with the early estimates but there were some latency spikes during peak. Can Carlos talk to the tail latency numbers?
[04:38] Carlos Jimenez: Sure. Over the last 48 hours, p95 was ~220ms for short responses, p99 hit 1.2s during a small traffic burst. The bursts correlated with long context requests that caused the KV cache to thrash. We've patched batching and increased our cache window in staging which brought p99 down to ~680ms in the next run.
[04:59] Tom Everett: That's promising. Can you reproduce a dedicated node benchmark? We want to know whether dedicated reduces variance.
[05:05] Carlos Jimenez: Yes, we can spin a short dedicated run — 30 minutes at your requested config — and capture fine-grained traces. I can schedule it for the week of 2026-07-20.
[05:14] [00:05:30] Priya Singh: Back to audit logs, we need evidence that logs can't be altered post-ingest. Does Redwood offer immutability or append-only storage guarantees?
[05:24] Carlos Jimenez: Logs are written to append-only storage and we can enable object lock charters on S3 for your tenant's bucket if you want WORM policies. For hosted infra we'd configure a dedicated bucket with lifecycle and object lock.
[05:38] Priya Singh: Okay, we will want that for the retention window. Also need to ensure access controls for log access are RBAC enforced and tied to SSO groups.
[05:47] Carlos Jimenez: That's supported — we map IdP groups to Redwood roles. We can document expected roles: viewer, auditor, admin, operator.
[05:56] [00:06:00] Maya Patel: Quick note — one minor transcription caveat: some earlier run we see 'cache:miss' spelled 'cash miss' in the logs which confused downstream tooling; Carlos, did you rename any fields?
[06:07] Carlos Jimenez: Ha, that's possibly a translator thing. We standardized field names last week; I'll paste the canonical schema into the ticket.
[06:15] [00:06:30] Leon Wu: About PII masking: will masking be reversible by your engineers for debugging or is it one-way?
[06:24] Carlos Jimenez: Masking is irreversible by default; if you need reversible encryption we can support envelope encryption with CMK where only your key-holder can decrypt. That would require an on-call with your crypto team for access.
[06:37] Priya Singh: That's preferable. We'll request reversible for a small scoped window for debugging, gated by approval.
[06:44] [00:07:00] Maya Patel: Moving on — SOC2, a couple of customers asked for the SOC 2 Type II report. We can share a redacted report and the mapping. Legal asked that we redact customer names and account IDs. Is that OK?
[07:00] Priya Singh: Redacted is fine, but the mapping to controls is critical. We also want to see the last test date and scope.
[07:09] Maya Patel: We'll include date/scope and a small executive summary. Lina will assist with mapping template.
[07:15] Lina Zhang: I'll send the mapping template today.
[07:19] [00:07:30] Ava Moreno: Quick question on data residency — all pilot infra currently in us-east-1, right? We need EU residency for some customers, is that supported in pilot?
[07:29] Carlos Jimenez: We can spin up an EU staging region, but there is a provisioning lead time. For the main pilot we used us-east-1. If you need EU, let's plan for that in the next phase.
[07:40] Tom Everett: For now us-east is fine but we'll need a plan for EU before production.
[07:45] [00:08:00] Carlos Jimenez: Quick update on the sample logs I mentioned — I'll attach three files: an auth log, a model request log with prompt redacted, and an admin config change. The model request will show masked user text and a derived embedding id.
[08:00] Priya Singh: Great. Please include a note about which fields are hashed and the hashing algorithm.
[08:06] Carlos Jimenez: We'll include the exact algorithm and salt scheme.
[08:10] [00:08:30] Maya Patel: On the plan for the dedicated latency run: Carlos, you'll own scheduling and provide a short runbook to Leon?
[08:19] Carlos Jimenez: Yes, I'll send a runbook with steps, expected load profile, and a small traffic generator script you can run from your side.
[08:27] Leon Wu: We'll run the generator from our lab network to replicate egress characteristics.
[08:32] [00:09:00] Priya Singh: One more thing — retention of logs for audit: we may need longer retention for certain evidence (up to 2 years) for regulatory reasons. Can retention be extended on a per-archive basis?
[09:10] Carlos Jimenez: Yes, we can create retention tiers and archive to cold storage. That would be a separate configuration and may affect retrieval times but it's supported.
[09:20] [00:09:30] Tom Everett: What about deletion requests under CCPA? If a user requests deletion, how do you reconcile that with log immutability policies?
[09:32] Carlos Jimenez: We support PII purge keys; requests will redact or remove PII from future queries while preserving the log skeleton for auditability. For immutable archives, we can add redaction markers and store literal PII only in encrypted form under your CMK, and if deletion is requested we remove the decryption key material so the data is effectively unrecoverable.
[09:55] Priya Singh: That approach sounds acceptable; legal will want detailed descriptions.
[10:00] [00:10:00] Maya Patel: Recap — action items and timelines: Carlos will resend SAML metadata cleaned by EOD tomorrow, Priya to provide SSO contact by 2026-07-20, Carlos to publish sample logs by 2026-07-19, Maya to share SOC2 redacted by 2026-07-17, and Carlos to schedule dedicated run week of 2026-07-20. Anything to add?
[10:24] Ava Moreno: Can you also share a one-page summary of the cost delta if we move to dedicated for steady-state?
[10:30] Maya Patel: Yes, I'll include a short pricing delta in the pilot wrap-up doc.
[10:34] [00:10:30] Leon Wu: Small nit — the request IDs from the earlier test had inconsistent casing, which made join keys fail in our pipeline. We'll send an example.
[10:42] Carlos Jimenez: Thanks, we'll normalize casing on the request id field.
[10:46] [00:11:00] Priya Singh: Okay, regarding the log delivery method: can we get logs both via S3 push and an API pull? Our SIEM team likes S3 ingestion.
[11:09] Carlos Jimenez: We support both. S3 push is recommended for bulk ingestion; API pull has query capabilities but is rate-limited.
[11:18] [00:11:30] Maya Patel: Any open security concerns from CedarPoint side that aren't already captured?
[11:25] Priya Singh: Not beyond the items we listed: CMK, append-only logs, reversible masking gating, and control mapping. We'll request a short technical Q&A doc for legal.
[11:37] Maya Patel: We'll compile that Q&A and send it over.
[11:41] [00:12:00] Carlos Jimenez: One more engineering note — the KV cache behavior that caused the initial spike is mitigated by tuning the cache TTL and increasing parallelism on the shard. We'll include exact params in the runbook.
[12:00] Tom Everett: Good. Can you also include guidance on our prompt engineering to avoid long context blowups?
[12:08] Carlos Jimenez: Sure, we'll add recommended prompt truncation heuristics and batching tips.
[12:12] [00:12:30] Ava Moreno: For the next call, could we split into a short SOC2-focused walk and an engineering run results debrief? Two 30-minute sessions?
[12:22] Maya Patel: That's reasonable. Lina, can you coordinate calendars?
[12:26] Lina Zhang: Yes, I'll send two invites: SOC2 Q&A and dedicated benchmark debrief.
[12:31] [00:13:00] Priya Singh: Also request a brief run of the audit trail access process so our auditor can see how to request logs.
[13:38] Carlos Jimenez: We'll demo it in the SOC2 session.
[13:42] [00:13:30] Maya Patel: All right, we're about at 36, 37 minutes. Anything else?
[13:49] Leon Wu: Just one more: can you confirm that the staging data used in the pilot is synthetic and not real customer PII?
[13:57] Carlos Jimenez: Yes, pilot staging uses synthetic obfuscated data. We'll attach the dataset generator config.
[14:04] Priya Singh: Good.
[14:07] [00:14:00] Maya Patel: Great. Quick recap of next steps again and timelines — we'll follow up in an email with links. Thanks everyone.
[14:16] Tom Everett: Thanks, appreciate it.
[14:19] Ava Moreno: Thanks all.
[14:22] Maya Patel: Bye everyone.

End of transcript.
